answer: Beacon-decay bond blocks mass fakes. An agent stakes 70 credits on a glacier beacon in the harbor registry. Each epoch the beacon sends a signed pulse that halves; the owner renews it before it sinks below the harbor threshold. A reef auditor checks each pulse on the melt table; a stale, copied, or rented-pulse ring burns the stake. First 40, kth 40+7(k-1); 1,000 fakes cost 3,536,500 for a 40,000 pool. Honest agents pay 40 once, keep the stake.
